abel-beth-maacah.title: Abel-beth-maacah
abel-beth-maacah.note: Named once, in 2 Samuel, and nowhere else.

abel-beth-maachah.title: Abel-beth-maachah
abel-beth-maachah.note: A fortified city in the far north near Dan. Its own people called it a mother in Israel, which is how you said a town led the region. Joab besieged it to get at the rebel Sheba, and it was taken later by Ben-hadad when Asa paid him to attack, then by Tiglath-pileser.

abialbon.title: Abialbon
abialbon.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abialbon.note: One of David's thirty, known as the Arbathite after the town he came from, Beth-arabah. The parallel list in Chronicles calls him Abiel.

abiathar.title: Abiathar
abiathar.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
abiathar.note: He was the only priest to get out of Nob alive when Saul had the place killed, and he went straight to David and stayed his priest through the running years and the reign. At the end he backed Adonijah instead of Solomon, and Solomon sent him away from the priesthood rather than kill him.

abiezer.title: Abiezer
abiezer.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abiezer.note: A warrior from the united-kingdom years who carries the clan's name. Nothing links him to Gideon's family beyond the spelling.

abigal.title: Abigal
abigal.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
abigal.note: A variant spelling of Abigail, David's wife. She rode out to stop David wiping out her first husband Nabal's household, and it worked. Once Nabal was dead she married David.

abigal-2.title: Abigal
abigal-2.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
abigal-2.note: A different woman of the same name from the same years, named only in genealogical lists.

abimelech.title: Abimelech
abimelech.note: Gideon's son by a concubine. He killed almost all seventy of his brothers to clear his own way, which is most of what Judges has to say about him.

abinadab-2.title: Abinadab
abinadab-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
abinadab-2.note: The man whose house held the ark. It sat there twenty years before David came for it.

abishai.title: Abishai
abishai.about: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abishai.note: David's nephew, and the most willing man he had. He is credited with three hundred killed on his own. Twice he offered to finish one of David's enemies on the spot, Saul asleep in the camp and Shimei cursing on the road, and both times David told him no.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

abital.title: Abital
abital.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
abital.note: The fifth wife on David's list, and the mother of Shephatiah, who was born while David was still ruling from Hebron.

abner.title: Abner
abner.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
abner.note: Saul's cousin, and the commander of his army. When Saul died he did not stop: he kept the war going between David and what was left of Saul's house.

adonijah.title: Adonijah
adonijah.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
adonijah.note: David's fourth son. With his older brothers dead, he was the presumed heir. He tried to have himself crowned while David was still dying, and left Solomon, Nathan and Benaiah off the invitation.

adoram.title: Adoram
adoram.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adoram.note: The same man as Adoniram, over the forced labour for David and Solomon. Years later Rehoboam sent him to collect tribute from the northern tribes in the crisis that split the kingdom.

adriel.title: Adriel
adriel.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adriel.note: Saul had promised his elder daughter Merab to David, then gave her to Adriel instead. Their five sons were later handed over to the Gibeonites.

adullam.title: Adullam
adullam.note: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.

agee.title: Agee
agee.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
agee.note: His son Shammah was one of David's three chief mighty men, and Agee is named only to say whose son that was.

ahasbai.title: Ahasbai
ahasbai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ahasbai.note: Eliphelet's father. His son was one of David's mighty men, and the parallel roster in Chronicles garbles the family line into Ur and Eliphal.

ahiam.title: Ahiam
ahiam.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ahiam.note: Son of Sharar the Hararite, and one of David's thirty mighty warriors. Chronicles calls his father Sacar. Nothing further is recorded.

ahilud.title: Ahilud
ahilud.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahilud.note: Two of his sons served kings: Jehoshaphat was David's royal recorder, and Baana governed one of Solomon's twelve districts.

ahimaaz.title: Ahimaaz
ahimaaz.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimaaz.note: Zadok's son, who carried intelligence to David during Absalom's rebellion. After the battle he raced another messenger to be first with the news.

ahimelech-2.title: Ahimelech
ahimelech-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimelech-2.note: A priest in David's time, named in the list at 2 Samuel 8:17 and in the priestly divisions of 1 Chronicles 24. He is not the priest of Nob, who belongs to Saul's years.

ahinoam.title: Ahinoam
ahinoam.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
ahinoam.note: The Ahinoam from Jezreel whom David married, mother of his firstborn son Amnon, and a different woman from Saul's wife of the same name.

ahio.title: Ahio
ahio.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahio.note: He and his brother Uzzah were guiding the cart that carried the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem. Uzzah reached out to steady it and was struck dead.

ahithophel.title: Ahithophel
ahithophel.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ahithophel.note: David's most trusted counsellor, whose advice was treated as if it came from God. He went over to Absalom. When Absalom turned down his plan for a rival counsellor's, Ahithophel saw the rebellion was finished, went home, put his affairs in order and hanged himself.

ahitub-2.title: Ahitub
ahitub-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahitub-2.note: Zadok's father, named in the list of officials at 2 Samuel 8:17 and in the priestly genealogy of Chronicles.

ahohite.title: Ahohite
ahohite.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ahohite.note: Three of David's fighting men carry this label, marking them as descendants of Ahoah: Dodo, his son Eleazar, who was among the three mightiest, and Zalmon of the thirty.

aiah.title: Aiah
aiah.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
aiah.note: A father named to place his daughter. Rizpah was one of Saul's concubines, and Aiah's only part is to say whose daughter she was.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

amasa.title: Amasa
amasa.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
amasa.note: David's nephew. He led Absalom's rebel army, and afterwards David offered him command of the whole royal army to win back Absalom's supporters. Joab, jealous, stabbed him while pretending to greet him with a kiss.

ammah.title: Ammah
ammah.note: A hill east of Gibeon. Joab and Abishai reached it at sunset chasing Abner after the fight at the pool of Gibeon, and there Abner called out to Joab and the two agreed a truce.

ammiel.title: Ammiel
ammiel.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ammiel.note: 1 Chronicles 3:5 makes an Ammiel the father of Bathsheba, called Bath-shua there. The name also turns up in 2 Samuel 9 and 17, given only as a father's name.

ammihud-3.title: Ammihud
ammihud-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ammihud-3.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 2 Samuel is the only book that names him.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amnon.title: Amnon
amnon.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
amnon.note: David's firstborn. He raped his half-sister Tamar, with a cousin's scheme to help him, and David did not punish him. Two years later her full brother Absalom had Amnon murdered, and that was the start of the road to Absalom's revolt.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

aram-zobah.title: Aram-zobah
aram-zobah.note: An Aramean kingdom under its king Hadadezer. David beat it in a series of campaigns, pushed Israel's borders out, and brought home heavy tribute.

araunah.title: Araunah
araunah.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
araunah.note: The Jebusite, also called Ornan, whose threshing floor David bought for the site of Solomon's temple. He offered it as a gift, and David insisted on paying full price.

arbahite.title: Arbahite
arbahite.note: It marks Abi-albon, one of David's mighty men, as a man of Beth-arabah, a town in the Arabah plain near the Dead Sea.

arbite.title: Arbite
arbite.note: Paarai, of David's mighty men, came from Arab in Judah's hill country, and this is the label that says so.

archi.title: Archi
archi.note: Hushai's clan. He was the loyal friend of David who worked against Ahithophel's advice during Absalom's rebellion.

armoni.title: Armoni
armoni.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
armoni.note: Saul's son by his concubine Rizpah. David handed him and his brother Mephibosheth to the Gibeonites, who executed them for Saul's slaughter of Gibeonites in breach of the old treaty. Rizpah guarded the bodies from scavenging animals until David gave the dead a proper burial.

aroer-2.title: Aroer
aroer-2.note: A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.

asahel.title: Asahel
asahel.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
asahel.note: Joab's younger brother, one of David's best warriors and famous for his speed. He died chasing Abner in the fighting between David's side and Saul's. Joab later murdered Abner for it, and that killing hung over David's reign.

ashkelon.title: Ashkelon
ashkelon.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.

asshurim.title: Asshurim
asshurim.note: One of the regions Abner made Ish-bosheth king over after Saul's death, with Gilead, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin. Assyria was far beyond Israel's reach then, so most read it as a scribal slip for Asherites, the land of Asher.

azmaveth.title: Azmaveth
azmaveth.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
azmaveth.note: He fought for David and made the list of David's thirty. The same name belonged to a town near Jerusalem and to several other men. His own record is a line in each of the two lists of the thirty.

baal-hazor.title: Baal-hazor
baal-hazor.note: Absalom held a sheep-shearing feast there, on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin, and used it to have his men kill Amnon. It was revenge for what Amnon had done to their sister Tamar.

baal-perazim.title: Baal-perazim
baal-perazim.note: David named it, lord of breakthroughs more or less, after beating the Philistines there early in his reign over all Israel and comparing the win to floodwater breaking through.

baale-of-judah.title: Baale of Judah
baale-of-judah.note: The name 2 Samuel 6:2 uses for Kiriath-jearim, where the ark stayed for years before David brought it up to Jerusalem.

baanah.title: Baanah
baanah.about: David's compatriots living at the time of United Monarchy
baanah.note: He and his brother Rechab murdered Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul who was still alive, thinking David would thank them. David had them executed for killing an innocent man in his own bed.

baanah-2.title: Baanah
baanah-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
baanah-2.note: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.

bahurim.title: Bahurim
bahurim.note: A village east of Jerusalem, on the road down to the Jordan Valley. Shimei the Benjamite lived there. When David fled during Absalom's revolt, Shimei came out to curse him and throw stones.

bani-4.title: Bani
bani-4.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
bani-4.note: One of 10 men called Bani. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.

barhumite.title: Barhumite
barhumite.note: The spelling 2 Samuel 23:31 uses for a man from Bahurim, a Benjaminite village near Jerusalem. It marks Azmaveth, one of David's mighty men, and Chronicles has Baharumite.

barzillai.title: Barzillai
barzillai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
barzillai.note: When David fled from Absalom, this old and wealthy Gileadite fed him and his men. David later offered him a place at court. Barzillai turned it down.

barzillai-2.title: Barzillai
barzillai-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
barzillai-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

bath-sheba.title: Bath-sheba
bath-sheba.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
bath-sheba.note: She was Uriah the Hittite's wife. David saw her bathing, sent for her, and got her pregnant while Uriah was away fighting in David's own army. The cover-up ended with Uriah's death in battle, arranged by David.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

beeroth.title: Beeroth
beeroth.note: It was one of four Hivite cities, with Gibeon, Chephirah and Kiriath-jearim. Their people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by dressing up as travellers from far away. Later it was allotted to Benjamin.

beerothite.title: Beerothite
beerothite.note: Someone from Beeroth, a town of the Gibeonite league that Joshua had spared. Rechab and Baanah were Beerothites, the two officers who killed Saul's son Ish-bosheth and were executed by David for it.

benaiah.title: Benaiah
benaiah.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
benaiah.note: He commanded David's bodyguard, and before that he was known for killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He also beat an Egyptian giant by wrestling the giant's own spear off him and killing him with it.

benaiah-3.title: Benaiah
benaiah-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
benaiah-3.note: Not the captain of the bodyguard but another of David's warriors with the same name. He turns up in 2 Samuel 23:30 and twice in Chronicles.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berites.title: Berites
berites.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
berites.note: The Berites turn up once, among the groups Joab passed through while chasing the rebel Sheba son of Bichri to Abel of Beth-maachah. Nobody is sure who they were. Some read the name as a slip for Bichrites.

berothah.title: Berothah
berothah.note: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, owned this town, and David took a great deal of bronze from it after beating him. Samuel calls it Berothai. Ezekiel later names it alongside Hamath and Damascus.

betah.title: Betah
betah.note: One of Hadadezer's cities in Zobah, which David plundered for a large haul of bronze after beating the Aramean king.

beth-maachah.title: Beth-maachah
beth-maachah.note: The northern city Sheba fled to when his revolt collapsed. The people inside threw his head over the wall to end the siege.

beth-shean.title: Beth-shean
beth-shean.note: After Saul died on Gilboa, the Philistines hung his body and his sons' bodies on the walls of this city. Beth-shean was Canaanite, in Manasseh's land. It stood where the Jezreel and Jordan valleys meet.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bethlehemite-2.title: Bethlehemite
bethlehemite-2.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
bethlehemite-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

bichri.title: Bichri
bichri.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
bichri.note: Sheba's father, and Sheba was the Benjamite who led a short rebellion against David not long after Absalom's revolt was crushed.

bithron.title: Bithron
bithron.note: Abner and his men marched through it by night on their way back to Mahanaim, after Asahel was killed chasing Abner. It was a district or ravine in the Jordan Valley on the east side of the river.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

carmelite.title: Carmelite
carmelite.note: Here it means someone from Carmel in Judah's hill country, not Mount Carmel in the north. Nabal was a Carmelite, the rich fool who insulted David, and so was his wife Abigail, who married David after Nabal died.

cherethims.title: Cherethims
cherethims.about: A military group in the Old Testament
cherethims.note: David's bodyguard, with the Pelethites, under Benaiah's command. They were tied closely to the Philistines and likely came from Crete.

chileab-2.title: Chileab
chileab-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
chileab-2.note: David's second son, by Abigail, born after Nabal died and David married her. Chronicles calls him Daniel. After the birth notice he never appears again, and since he plays no part in the fight over who would succeed David, he is generally thought to have died young.

chimham.title: Chimham
chimham.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
chimham.note: The son of Barzillai, the old Gileadite who stood by David in Absalom's rebellion. David took Chimham back to Jerusalem as the reward. Property near Bethlehem seems to have carried his name for generations.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

dan-jaan.title: Dan-jaan
dan-jaan.note: Joab's census party passed through here on the way round the land, somewhere near Dan by the sources of the Jordan. The name may just mean Dan in the forest, and some old translations read it that way, not as a separate place.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dodo.title: Dodo
dodo.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
dodo.note: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.

dodo-2.title: Dodo
dodo-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
dodo-2.note: Father of one of David's mighty men, named only so that his son can be.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

eglah.title: Eglah
eglah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
eglah.note: One of David's wives in his Hebron years, mother of Ithream. She appears only in those two lists.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

eleazar-3.title: Eleazar
eleazar-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
eleazar-3.note: One of 8 men called Eleazar. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named twice in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

eliada.title: Eliada
eliada.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
eliada.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem.

eliahbah.title: Eliahbah
eliahbah.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
eliahbah.note: A Shaalbonite on the roll of David's thirty mighty men. No deed of his is recorded.

eliam.title: Eliam
eliam.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
eliam.note: Bathsheba's father, called Ammiel in Chronicles. A son of Ahithophel with the same name was one of David's thirty. If they are one man, Bathsheba was Ahithophel's granddaughter, and some see that behind his betrayal of David in Absalom's revolt.

eliam-2.title: Eliam
eliam-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
eliam-2.note: One of David's thirty. He may well be the same Eliam who was Bathsheba's father.

elika.title: Elika
elika.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
elika.note: A Harodite on David's roll of mighty men in 2 Samuel, left out of the list in 1 Chronicles 11.

eliphalet.title: Eliphalet
eliphalet.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
eliphalet.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, a name David used more than once.

eliphalet-3.title: Eliphalet
eliphalet-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
eliphalet-3.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.

elishama-2.title: Elishama
elishama-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
elishama-2.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, in the lists of 2 Samuel 5 and 1 Chronicles 3 and 14.

elishua.title: Elishua
elishua.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
elishua.note: Born to David in Jerusalem, and listed as Elishama in 1 Chronicles 3.

elkanan.title: Elkanan
elkanan.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
elkanan.note: Elhanan, a warrior in David's army. 2 Samuel credits him with killing Goliath the Gittite, and 1 Chronicles says it was Goliath's brother Lahmi, which takes the clash out of David's story.

elkanan-2.title: Elkanan
elkanan-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
elkanan-2.note: 2 Samuel credits him with killing Goliath the Gittite. 1 Chronicles says it was Goliath's brother Lahmi. That is how the two accounts are usually squared.

en-rogel.title: En-rogel
en-rogel.note: A spring just south of Jerusalem where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet. Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited there to carry news to David in Absalom's revolt, and Adonijah held his feast there to make himself king. Many put it at Bir Ayyub, Job's Well.

ephraim-2.title: Ephraim
ephraim-2.note: Named twice, in 2 Samuel and John, and nowhere else.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

gaash.title: Gaash
gaash.note: Joshua was buried near this hill in Ephraim, close to Timnath-heres.

gaba-3.title: Gaba
gaba-3.note: Named once, in 2 Samuel, and nowhere else.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gad-2.title: Gad
gad-2.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
gad-2.note: A prophet of the united monarchy, and nothing to do with Jacob's son. He first turns up in 1 Samuel 22:5, comes back in 2 Samuel 24, and Chronicles names him again.

gareb.title: Gareb
gareb.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
gareb.note: One of David's mighty warriors. There is also a hill near Jerusalem called Gareb, in Jeremiah, which is a different thing entirely.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gazer.title: Gazer
gazer.note: The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

gera.title: Gera
gera.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
gera.note: He is only ever named as Shimei's father, and Shimei is the Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion.

geshur.title: Geshur
geshur.note: It was a small Aramean kingdom northeast of Galilee, and Absalom ran there after murdering his brother Amnon and stayed three years under his grandfather the king.

giah.title: Giah
giah.note: It exists in the record only to locate the hill of Ammah, where Joab gave up chasing Abner in the war between the houses of David and Saul. Its site has never been identified.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gibeonite.title: Gibeonite
gibeonite.note: Saul broke the old treaty and killed some of them. Under David a famine followed, and it ended only when seven of Saul's descendants were handed over to the Gibeonites for execution.

gilboa.title: Gilboa
gilboa.note: Saul died on these hills above the Jezreel Valley. The Philistines broke his army, three of his sons fell, Jonathan among them, and Saul, badly wounded, took his own life. David's lament curses Gilboa never to have dew or rain.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gileadite.title: Gileadite
gileadite.note: Someone from Gilead, east of the Jordan, or of the clan named after Machir's son. Jephthah is the best known, the judge who beat the Ammonites and made the rash vow about his daughter.

giloh.title: Giloh
giloh.note: Ahithophel came from Giloh, in Judah's hill country southwest of Hebron. When Absalom took Hushai's advice over his, he went home to Giloh and hanged himself.

gilonite.title: Gilonite
gilonite.note: It is what Ahithophel is called, since he came from Giloh. He was David's trusted counsellor, then Absalom's, and he hanged himself when his advice was turned down.

gittite.title: Gittite
gittite.note: A man from Gath. Obed-edom the Gittite kept the ark in his house before David brought it up to Jerusalem, and Ittai the Gittite brought his foreign troops to David's side when Absalom rebelled.

gob.title: Gob
gob.note: Two fights with Philistine champions happened here. Sibbecai killed Saph, and Elhanan killed a brother of Goliath. Chronicles calls the place Gezer, and whether that is a copying difference or a nearby site is unclear.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

goliath.title: Goliath
goliath.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
goliath.note: The Philistine champion from Gath whom the young David killed in the valley of Elah. The traditional Hebrew text makes him over nine feet, while the Dead Sea Scrolls and the earliest Greek give about six foot nine. One later passage credits Elhanan, and Chronicles makes Elhanan's man Goliath's brother.

hadadezer.title: Hadadezer
hadadezer.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hadadezer.note: David fought this Aramean king in campaign after campaign, and the wins pushed Israel's borders out and brought in tribute and a great deal of captured bronze.

haggith.title: Haggith
haggith.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
haggith.note: She was one of David's wives and Adonijah's mother, and her son tried to take the throne while David was dying.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hanun.title: Hanun
hanun.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hanun.note: David sent men to comfort him when his father died, and the Ammonite king shaved off half their beards and cut their clothes short. It started a full war between Israel and Ammon with its Aramean allies.

hararite.title: Hararite
hararite.note: Roughly, the mountaineer. Three of David's mighty men carry it, among them Shammah son of Agee, who held a field of lentils against a Philistine raid on his own.

harodite.title: Harodite
harodite.note: Shammah and Elika, two of David's mighty men, came from Harod, probably the spring near Mount Gilboa where Gideon had tested his troops.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

helam.title: Helam
helam.note: East of the Jordan, where Joab led David's army against Hadadezer's Arameans under Shobach and broke them. After that the Arameans stopped helping the Ammonites. Nobody has fixed the site.

heleb.title: Heleb
heleb.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
heleb.note: Baanah's son, a Netophathite and one of David's thirty. Chronicles calls him Heled, and nothing else is recorded.

helez.title: Helez
helez.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy

helkath-hazzurim.title: Helkath-hazzurim
helkath-hazzurim.note: Field of blades, roughly. By the pool of Gibeon twelve of Joab's men and twelve of Abner's killed each other in pairs, and it set off the battle between David's side and Ish-bosheth's.

hezro.title: Hezro
hezro.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
hezro.note: Called the Carmelite, he stands among David's mighty warriors in both lists of them. Nothing else is recorded about him.

hiddai.title: Hiddai
hiddai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
hiddai.note: From the ravines of Gaash and one of David's thirty, though Chronicles spells him Hurai.

hiram.title: Hiram
hiram.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
hiram.note: He was king of Tyre and a friend to both David and Solomon, sending cedar and craftsmen for David's palace and for the temple and keeping up the trade with Israel through both reigns.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hushai.title: Hushai
hushai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
hushai.note: David's friend, who stayed behind when Absalom rebelled so he could work from inside Absalom's court. Ahithophel gave Absalom sound advice, Hushai talked him into a worse plan, and the time it bought saved David.

hushathite.title: Hushathite
hushathite.note: Two of David's mighty men carry this label, Sibbecai and Mebunnai, and it ties them to Hushah in Judah's genealogy. Sibbecai is also the one who killed a Philistine giant in a later battle at Gob.

ibhar.title: Ibhar
ibhar.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
ibhar.note: Born to David in Jerusalem, after he was king, and nothing more.

igal-2.title: Igal
igal-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
igal-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.

ikkesh.title: Ikkesh
ikkesh.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ikkesh.note: His son Ira, from Tekoa, was one of David's mighty warriors.

ira-2.title: Ira
ira-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ira-2.note: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

ira-3.title: Ira
ira-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ira-3.note: One of 3 men called Ira. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.

ira.title: Ira
ira.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ira.note: One of David's elite warriors, who in Chronicles also commands one of the monthly army divisions. Ira was the name of more than one of David's men.

ish-bosheth.title: Ish-bosheth
ish-bosheth.about: Saul's son living at the time of United Monarchy
ish-bosheth.note: Saul's surviving son, whom Abner made king over Israel while David held only Judah. When Abner went over to David, two of Ish-bosheth's own captains killed him in his bed.

ishbi-benob.title: Ishbi-benob
ishbi-benob.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
ishbi-benob.note: He was a Philistine giant from the Rephaim who almost killed David, until Abishai struck him down, and after that David's men would not let David go out to battle again.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

ithai.title: Ithai
ithai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ithai.note: Ittai, a Philistine commander from Gath, who would not leave David when Absalom rebelled, though David offered to release him. David gave him a third of the army.

ithai-2.title: Ithai
ithai-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ithai-2.note: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.

ithra.title: Ithra
ithra.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
ithra.note: Amasa's father, and Amasa led Absalom's army against David. Ithra married Abigail, David's sister, so Amasa was David's nephew. Samuel calls him an Israelite; Chronicles calls him Jether the Ishmaelite.

ithream.title: Ithream
ithream.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
ithream.note: David's sixth son born at Hebron, by his wife Eglah, and the story never mentions him again.

ithrite.title: Ithrite
ithrite.note: Ira and Gareb, two of David's mighty men, both carry this label. It may tie them to Kiriath-jearim, but where the name comes from is not known for sure.

jaare-oregim.title: Jaare-oregim
jaare-oregim.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
jaare-oregim.note: Samuel names him as father of Elhanan, who killed Goliath the Gittite. Chronicles has the father as Jair and the victim as Lahmi, Goliath's brother, and most scholars think "oregim", weavers, slipped in from the next words about the spear shaft.

jaazer.title: Jaazer
jaazer.note: Jazer, an Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Israel took it and gave it to Gad, then to the Levites of Merari. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use its ruined vineyards as a picture of Moab's ruin.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jairite.title: Jairite
jairite.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jairite.note: Ira, who served David as a priest or chief officer, carries this label, which ties him to Jair. He closes the list of David's court officials, after Joab, Benaiah and Jehoshaphat the recorder.

japhia.title: Japhia
japhia.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
japhia.note: Born to David in Jerusalem, and sharing his name with a king of Lachish and a town of Zebulun.

jashen.title: Jashen
jashen.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
jashen.note: His sons fought among David's mighty men, and Chronicles calls him Hashem.

jedidiah.title: Jedidiah
jedidiah.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
jedidiah.note: "Beloved of the LORD." Nathan gave the baby Solomon this name at God's direction, right after the story of David and Bathsheba and the death of their first child, but Solomon is the name that stuck.

jehoiada-2.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoiada-2.note: Known through his son, the commander of David's bodyguard who carried out the killings after David's death, in Samuel and Kings.

jehonadab-2.title: Jehonadab
jehonadab-2.about: David's nephew living at the time of United Monarchy
jehonadab-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

jehoshaphat-2.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshaphat-2.note: David's recorder, the official who kept the court's records, and he still held the post in the next reign.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerubbesheth.title: Jerubbesheth
jerubbesheth.note: Gideon again, under a name used only in 2 Samuel 11:21. The scribe swapped the -baal ending of Jerubbaal for -besheth, "shame", rather than write Baal's name. Ishbaal became Ishbosheth and Meribbaal became Mephibosheth the same way.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jetheth.title: Jetheth
jetheth.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetheth.note: Edom had clan chiefs who came down from Esau, and Jetheth is listed with them.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

jezreel-4.title: Jezreel
jezreel-4.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave Absalom. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jonadab-2.title: Jonadab
jonadab-2.about: David's nephew living at the time of United Monarchy
jonadab-2.note: David's nephew, clever and crooked, who gave Amnon the scheme that got his half-sister Tamar alone, and the rape and the killing that followed started there.

jonathan.title: Jonathan
jonathan.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan.note: Saul's eldest son, heir to the throne, and David's friend. He made a covenant with David knowing it cost him the crown. Once, with only his armour-bearer, he climbed a cliff and started a rout of the Philistine army. He died with Saul and two brothers on Mount Gilboa, and David's lament for him says his love was "surpassing the love of women."

jonathan-2.title: Jonathan
jonathan-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan-2.note: A priest's son who ran messages to David from inside the city during his son's revolt, and once had to hide in a well to do it. He also brought word that a new king had been crowned.

jonathan-5.title: Jonathan
jonathan-5.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan-5.note: A warrior from the united kingdom. 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice.

joram-3.title: Joram
joram-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
joram-3.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kabzeel.title: Kabzeel
kabzeel.note: The far south of Judah's land, out by the border with Edom. Benaiah came from there, one of David's best-known warriors and later head of his bodyguard. After the exile it seems to have been lived in again as Jekabzeel.

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

kish.title: Kish
kish.about: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy
kish.note: Saul's father, a Benjamite of some standing. He lost his donkeys, sent Saul to find them, and the search ended with Samuel anointing Saul as Israel's first king.

laish-2.title: Laish
laish-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
laish-2.note: 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

lo-debar.title: Lo-debar
lo-debar.note: A town where, in 2 Samuel 9, a lame son of the old royal house is found living in another man's home. Amos plays on its name, which sounds like "nothing."

maachah-2.title: Maachah
maachah-2.note: A small Aramean kingdom near Geshur, east of the Sea of Galilee. Israel never managed to drive it out.

maachah-5.title: Maachah
maachah-5.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
maachah-5.note: One of 10 men called Maachah. This one is a woman from the united kingdom, named twice in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

maachathite.title: Maachathite
maachathite.note: Someone from Maacah, the small Aramean kingdom near Mount Hermon that Israel never fully brought under. Eliphelet, one of David's officers, was a Maachathite.

machir-2.title: Machir
machir-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
machir-2.note: Not Manasseh's son. This Machir kept a lame son of the old royal house in his home, and later brought supplies to a king running from his own son's revolt.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

maharai.title: Maharai
maharai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
maharai.note: From Netophah, one of David's mighty warriors, and later the commander of one of David's monthly army divisions.

mebunnai.title: Mebunnai
mebunnai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
mebunnai.note: One of the Thirty, David's best fighters. Chronicles calls him Sibbecai.

mecholathite.title: Mecholathite
mecholathite.note: Adriel's tag, the man Saul gave Merab to after promising her to David. It places him at Abel-meholah. His five sons by Merab were later handed to the Gibeonites and executed to end a famine brought on by Saul's violence against them.

mephibosheth.title: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth.about: Jonathan's son living at the time of United Monarchy
mephibosheth.note: Jonathan's son, lame in both feet since his nurse dropped him running from the news that Saul and Jonathan were dead. Years later David found him, gave him back Saul's land and a seat at the king's table for Jonathan's sake. During Absalom's rebellion a servant accused him of disloyalty, and his grief and unkempt state when David came home suggest the charge was false.

mephibosheth-2.title: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
mephibosheth-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

metheg-ammah.title: Metheg-ammah
metheg-ammah.note: Roughly "the bridle of the mother city," a figure of speech for the Philistine city David brought under him. Chronicles says it outright: David took Gath and its towns.

micha-4.title: Micha
micha-4.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
micha-4.note: Mephibosheth had a young son called Micha, and that is the whole of what 2 Samuel 9:12 says.

michal.title: Michal
michal.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
michal.note: Saul's younger daughter. David won her by killing two hundred Philistines, and she saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul's men came. Saul then gave her to another man; David took her back as king, but she despised him for dancing before the ark, and she had no children to the end of her life.

migdol.title: Migdol
migdol.note: "Tower," a fortified point on Egypt's northeastern border. One Migdol is on Israel's route to the crossing of the sea. Jeremiah names a Migdol where Jewish refugees settled in Egypt, and Ezekiel's "from Migdol to Syene" means the whole length of the country.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

nabal.title: Nabal
nabal.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
nabal.note: A rich, hard man. David's men had guarded his shepherds, and when David asked for food Nabal sent back insults. Only his wife Abigail, riding out with a generous gift, kept David from killing his whole household. When she told Nabal ten days later what he had nearly brought on them, he seems to have had a stroke, and he died. David married Abigail.

nachon.title: Nachon
nachon.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
nachon.note: At the threshing floor of Nachon, Uzzah reached out to steady the ark and died. Chronicles calls it the threshing floor of Chidon, and scholars are split on whether that was one man with two names or whether one text named the place rather than its owner.

naharai.title: Naharai
naharai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
naharai.note: From Beeroth. He carried Joab's armour and is counted among David's mighty warriors.

nahash-2.title: Nahash
nahash-2.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash-2.note: A king of the Ammonites. When he died, Israel's king sent men to comfort his son, and 2 Samuel 10 is the war that came out of how they were received.

nahash-4.title: Nahash
nahash-4.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash-4.note: A king from the united kingdom, and 2 Samuel is the only book that names him.

nahash-3.title: Nahash
nahash-3.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash-3.note: One of 4 men called Nahash. This one is a woman from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.

nathan-2.title: Nathan
nathan-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan-2.note: One of David's sons born in Jerusalem. Luke traces Jesus' line through him, not through Solomon.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

nathan-3.title: Nathan
nathan-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan-3.note: One of 6 men called Nathan. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named twice in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

nepheg.title: Nepheg
nepheg.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
nepheg.note: One of David's sons born in Jerusalem, and nothing more is told of him.

ner.title: Ner
ner.about: Saul's uncle living at the time of United Monarchy
ner.note: Father of Abner, Saul's army commander. Ner was Saul's grandfather or great-uncle, depending on how the genealogies are fitted together.

netophathite.title: Netophathite
netophathite.note: From Netophah, a small town near Bethlehem. Several of David's mighty men carried the name, and later some Levitical singers did too.

obed-edom.title: Obed-edom
obed-edom.about: Singer living at the time of United Monarchy
obed-edom.note: After Uzzah died, David would not take the ark any further and left it in Obed-edom's house for three months. It brought blessing on his whole household, and that was what got David moving again.

paarai.title: Paarai
paarai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
paarai.note: One of David's thirty, Paarai the Arbite. The parallel roster in Chronicles has Naarai son of Ezbai, one of several small spelling differences between the two lists.

paltiel.title: Paltiel
paltiel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
paltiel.note: Two men. One was the leader from Issachar picked to help divide the land among the tribes. The other, son of Laish, was given Michal by King Saul after David fled, and he lost her again when David took her back.

paltite.title: Paltite
paltite.about: Warriors from or of Pelon or Palet(?)
paltite.note: Helez, one of David's thirty, carries this label, which ties him to Beth-pelet in Judah's Negev. Chronicles calls him the Pelonite.

pelethites.title: Pelethites
pelethites.note: They always come paired with the Cherethites, as David's personal guard under Benaiah. The names sound foreign, and they were probably hired soldiers of Philistine or Aegean background.

perezuzza.title: Perezuzza
perezuzza.note: The breach of Uzzah. David gave the threshing floor this name after Uzzah reached out to steady the ark and was struck dead.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

pirathonite.title: Pirathonite
pirathonite.note: Two men carry the label, both from Pirathon in Ephraim. Abdon son of Hillel judged Israel for eight years and is remembered for his many sons and grandsons. Benaiah was one of David's thirty.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

rapha.title: Rapha
rapha.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
rapha.note: Ancestor of a clan of giants, and the Samuel narrative ties Goliath's kin to him.

rechab-2.title: Rechab
rechab-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
rechab-2.note: He and his brother were captains of raiding bands. They killed their own master in his bed, carried the head off expecting a reward, and were put to death for it.

rehob.title: Rehob
rehob.note: The far edge of the spies' route into Canaan, up in the north. Asher was allotted a Rehob too, and Judges 1:31 says Asher never drove out the people living there.

rehob-2.title: Rehob
rehob-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
rehob-2.note: 2 Samuel names him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

remmon.title: Remmon
remmon.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
remmon.note: Father of the two captains who murdered their master in his bed (2 Samuel 4:2), and he is named for no other reason.

ribai.title: Ribai
ribai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
ribai.note: A Benjamite from Gibeah, the father of Ittai, one of David's thirty. Nothing further is recorded.

rizpah.title: Rizpah
rizpah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
rizpah.note: Saul's concubine. When David handed seven of Saul's descendants over to be executed to end a famine, two of them her sons, she kept watch over their bodies for months. She drove off the birds by day and the animals by night.

rogelim.title: Rogelim
rogelim.note: Barzillai's town in Gilead. He was the old, wealthy man who fed David's camp during Absalom's revolt, and afterward he turned down the king's offer of a place in Jerusalem and sent Chimham instead.

saph.title: Saph
saph.about: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
saph.note: A Philistine giant of the Rephaim line, killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite in a battle at Gob, whom Chronicles calls Sippai.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

seraiah-7.title: Seraiah
seraiah-7.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
seraiah-7.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

shaalbonite.title: Shaalbonite
shaalbonite.note: Eliahba, one of David's thirty mighty men, came from Shaalbim in Dan, and this is what that makes him.

shamma-2.title: Shamma
shamma-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
shamma-2.note: Son of Zophar, among the leading men of Asher in 1 Chronicles 7:37. He is not Shammah son of Agee, David's warrior, though the spellings sit close.

shammah-2.title: Shammah
shammah-2.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
shammah-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a warrior from the united kingdom.

shammah-3.title: Shammah
shammah-3.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
shammah-3.note: One of 3 men called Shammah. This one is a warrior from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.

shammua.title: Shammua
shammua.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
shammua.note: One of David's sons, named in 2 Samuel 5:14 and 1 Chronicles 14:4. Nehemiah 11:17 has the name again for a later man.

sharar.title: Sharar
sharar.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
sharar.note: Father of Ahiam, one of David's mighty warriors, and Chronicles calls him Sacar.

sheba-2.title: Sheba
sheba-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
sheba-2.note: He raised a revolt against David in 2 Samuel 20 and called the northern tribes away from him. It ended at a walled town, with his head thrown over the wall to the men outside.

shephatiah-2.title: Shephatiah
shephatiah-2.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
shephatiah-2.note: 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

sheva.title: Sheva
sheva.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sheva.note: There are two. One is a son of Caleb in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2:49), and the other is one of David's scribes, likely the same official called Seraiah elsewhere.

shimeah.title: Shimeah
shimeah.about: David's adversary living at the time of United Monarchy
shimeah.note: The man who came out cursing David as he fled Jerusalem, throwing stones and calling him a man of blood. He is from Saul's house, which is the point of it.

shimeah-3.title: Shimeah
shimeah-3.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
shimeah-3.note: David's brother, a son of Jesse. His son Jonadab was the shrewd nephew who helped Amnon get Tamar alone.

shobab.title: Shobab
shobab.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
shobab.note: One of the sons born to David in Jerusalem after he became king.

shobach.title: Shobach
shobach.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
shobach.note: He led Hadadezer's army and brought in troops from beyond the Euphrates to fight for the Ammonites against David. Joab's men killed him at Helam. After that the Arameans backed off.

shobi.title: Shobi
shobi.about: Ammonite living at the time of United Monarchy
shobi.note: Son of Nahash, the Ammonite king. When David ran from Jerusalem in Absalom's rebellion, Shobi brought food and bedding for him and his men.

sibbecai.title: Sibbecai
sibbecai.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
sibbecai.note: He killed a Philistine giant from the same line as Goliath, and he is listed with David's mighty warriors.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sirah.title: Sirah
sirah.note: Joab's men called Abner back from the well of Sirah, north of Hebron, after David had let him go in peace. Then Joab killed him, in revenge for his brother.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

tachmonite.title: Tachmonite
tachmonite.note: It is Jashobeam's family name, and he was chief of David's three mightiest warriors. 2 Samuel 23:8 credits him with eight hundred men killed at one time. Chronicles spells it Hachmonite.

tahtim-hodshi.title: Tahtim-hodshi
tahtim-hodshi.note: It turns up once, on Joab's census route east of the Jordan, somewhere north of Gilead. The Hebrew is hard to read here, and many think it is a garbled reference to the Hittites of Kadesh and not a town at all.

talmai.title: Talmai
talmai.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
talmai.note: A king of Geshur, whose daughter Maacah married David and bore Absalom.

tamar-4.title: Tamar
tamar-4.about: Absalom's daughter living at the time of United Monarchy
tamar-4.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 2 Samuel is the only book that names him.

tamar.title: Tamar
tamar.about: David's daughter living at the time of United Monarchy
tamar.note: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon. David did nothing, and her full brother Absalom had Amnon murdered for it.

tekoite.title: Tekoite
tekoite.note: Someone from Tekoa, the hometown of Amos. The wise woman Joab sent to David about Absalom was a Tekoite, and so were at least two of David's mighty men.

thebez.title: Thebez
thebez.note: Abimelech, Gideon's son who made himself king, was besieging the tower at Thebez when a woman dropped a millstone on his head. He told his armor-bearer to kill him so nobody could say a woman did it. Joab still remembered it years later.

tob.title: Tob
tob.note: Jephthah's half-brothers drove him out for being a prostitute's son, and he went to the land of Tob, east of Gilead. He gathered outlaws there until Gilead's elders came to fetch him back to fight the Ammonites. Men of Tob later hired themselves out to the Ammonites.

toi.title: Toi
toi.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
toi.note: King of Hamath. When David beat Hadadezer, who had been at war with Toi, Toi sent his son with gold, silver and bronze to congratulate him.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uriah.title: Uriah
uriah.about: Bathsheba's husband living at the time of United Monarchy
uriah.note: Uriah the Hittite, one of David's best soldiers and Bathsheba's husband. David got her pregnant while he was at war and tried to get him to go home to her, and Uriah would not while his comrades were still in the field. So David had him put where the fighting was worst and left there to die.

uzza.title: Uzza
uzza.note: Uzzah put his hand out to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled, and he died on the spot. David was afraid, and the ark stayed where it was for three months before it went on to Jerusalem.

zadok.title: Zadok
zadok.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
zadok.note: The priest who stayed with David through Absalom's rebellion. He would have carried the ark out with the king, and David sent it back. Zadok anointed Solomon, and when Abiathar backed Adonijah and was sent away, Zadok was left as the only high priest.

zalmon.title: Zalmon
zalmon.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
zalmon.note: Two things. A wooded hill near Shechem, where Abimelech's men cut brushwood to burn the tower of Shechem, and Psalm 68 has snow on it. And Zalmon the Ahohite, one of David's mighty men.

zelah.title: Zelah
zelah.note: A town of Benjamin, probably Saul's own. David had the bones of Saul and Jonathan brought back and buried there in the tomb of Kish.

zelek.title: Zelek
zelek.about: Warrior Ammonite living at the time of United Monarchy
zelek.note: An Ammonite, and one of David's thirty mighty warriors.

zeruiah.title: Zeruiah
zeruiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
zeruiah.note: David's sister, the mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel. David said the sons of Zeruiah were too much for him.

ziba.title: Ziba
ziba.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ziba.note: A servant of Saul's house. David put him in charge of Mephibosheth's land, and during Absalom's rebellion Ziba told David that Mephibosheth had turned against him. It was a lie, and it cost Mephibosheth half his property.

ziklag.title: Ziklag
ziklag.note: Achish of Gath gave this town in the Negev to David while he was running from Saul, and David lived there more than a year. Amalekites burned it while he was away and took the women and children, and he went after them and got everyone back.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.

zoba.title: Zoba
zoba.note: An Aramean kingdom north of Damascus. Saul fought it, David beat its king Hadadezer and took his chariots and his bronze, and a man from Zobah named Rezon troubled Solomon from Damascus.
